# 2 Baruch Chapter 40 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 40 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 40:3 — "preserved / survive"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-I-also be-preserved" | Same preservation verb used in 25:1 for Baruch |
| LOGOS | "will I also be preserved" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "will I myself survive" | More natural modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "preserved" (EMET/LOGOS). This is the same divine preservation vocabulary used at 25:1 ("You will be kept/preserved until that time"). Terminological consistency is important.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Terminological consistency.

---

## 40:4 — "Whatever will be with you / what will become of others"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Whatever-will-be with-you, you-will-not-know" | Literal: "with you" could mean "what will happen to you" or "alongside you" |
| LOGOS | "Whatever will be with you — you will not know" | Same ambiguity preserved |
| PNEUMA | "What will become of others — that you will not know" | Interprets the ambiguity toward "others" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS's reading. The Syriac is genuinely ambiguous. LOGOS preserves the ambiguity while PNEUMA resolves it. SOPHIA prefers to preserve the ambiguity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Ambiguity preserved.

---
